text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner states the car rides comfortably and is easy to handle. Owner states the car almost drives itself thanks to its many electronics. Owner says this is their fifth E-Class and all previous ones were reliable and safe. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «almost drives itself»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner states the EQE 350+ sedan is very fast. Owner states the car is very comfortable. Owner reports more than 360 miles per charge, depending on driving habits. Owner calls the EQE possibly the best EV sedan in its class.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner finds the interior luxurious, with good lighting and technology. Owner finds the interior spacious with good storage. Owner finds the exterior sleek, although nothing about it stands out. Owner states acceleration is smooth and performance is strong. Owner states the car handles well. Owner reports about 360 miles of real-world range per charge, mostly on the highway. Owner reports the car repeatedly failed to connect to Electrify America chargers, showing errors, especially below about 30 % charge, while other cars charged fine; the dealer could not find the cause. Owner states DC charging from 10 % to full takes about 45-50 minutes. Owner finds the ride firmer than their previous Mercedes GLE because the EQE sits lower.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2023 EQE 500 especially likes the twilight blue paint. Owner appreciates the extra features of the EQE 500 trim. Owner reports electrical problems that have kept the car in the shop for three weeks, and says Mercedes is still working out bugs in the EQ line.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner states that at about 4,000 miles several warning lights came on, the car became undrivable and had to be towed to the dealer. Owner states fuel economy is poor compared with their previous 2017 G80. Owner states the controls are hard to use while driving. Owner describes the car as beautiful (review title) despite the reliability problems.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the tight handling and the ride quality on rough roads. Owner praises the fuel economy. Owner states the car is easy to operate. Owner praises the sound system. Owner praises the low road noise in the cabin.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a G80 3.5T, who traded in a Porsche Panamera, praises the car's style. Owner praises the interior. Owner praises the driving experience. Owner praises the features and calls it the best buy for the money.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner states the car suits the family, with plenty of rear legroom and comfort for the children. Owner praises the many options and features and rates it above a Mercedes they owned.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): New owner states it is a great car and they are very happy with it.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the looks of the car. Owner states the warranty tipped the purchase decision over another car they considered (a '350e', brand not named).

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner states problems began at under 10,000 miles after a fuel injector replacement; the car was towed to the shop three times in three months and spent 7 of 12 weeks there. Owner states parts, including a battery, were slow to arrive and customer service apologized but did not resolve the issues. Owner praises the design and style of the car despite its unreliability. Owner praises the comfort of the car.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Third-time G80 owner praises the comfort. Owner praises the technology in the car. Owner praises the safety of the car. Owner states they like the exterior styling less than their previous 2017 G80. Owner states prices have risen, so the G80 is no longer as good a value deal as before. Owner states CarPlay music no longer shows all artists or playlists, forcing them to use the phone instead.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the power of the car. Owner praises the infotainment system, including the drive-mode selection and the navigation screen. Owner praises the radar-based lane-following assist (described by the owner as hands-off) and the lane-line warnings. Owner, replacing a Cadillac XT5, praises the comfort.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a used 2023 G80 praises the fuel economy in Eco mode. Owner praises the power available in Sport mode. Owner praises the smooth ride. Owner praises the comfortable seats. Owner praises the technology in the car.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a used 2022 G80 Sport Prestige praises the build quality. Owner praises the rear-wheel steering. Owner praises the soft-close doors. Owner praises the comfortable seats. Owner praises the interior. Owner states the dealer's parts and service delays lasted about five months and calls the dealer service atrocious. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «atrocious dealer service»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2022 ES 300h Ultra Luxury praises the exterior design. Owner praises the interior design. Owner praises the spacious, comfortable cabin and the adjustable seat height. Owner praises the Mark Levinson audio system. Owner notes a noticeable acceleration lag at low speeds. Owner gets about 40.7 mpg versus the advertised 43-44 mpg.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a used ES finds the mouse-style controller distracting while driving. Owner finds the instrument cluster confusing. Owner states the navigation repeatedly routes to an old destination. Owner finds headroom limited and the low sporty seats hard for an older driver to get out of. Owner complains there is only one cup holder and misses the sunglasses compartment of their previous Avalon. Owner reports paint chips after a single highway trip. Owner likes the heated seats and heated steering wheel. Owner likes the safety features.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of an ES with the Luxury package praises the ride. Owner praises the quietness of the cabin. Owner reports 31-34 mpg on the highway on regular fuel. Owner praises the roomy interior and large trunk. Owner dislikes the mouse-style touchpad for operating the display. Owner wants heated rear seats.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a new 2022 ES 300h states the rear speakers are nearly silent and the rear subwoofer produces no output, and the dealer did not respond.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a certified pre-owned 2019 ES 350 praises the ride comfort. Owner praises the quietness. Owner praises the power. Owner finds the stereo below expectations for a luxury car. Owner reports a 2-3 hour service visit despite an appointment and unanswered callback requests.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a used 2019 ES 350 complains the steering-wheel buttons have no tactile features. Owner reports a steering-wheel control bug that changes radio presets unpredictably. Owner finds the trunk opening and cargo space limited. Owner finds getting in and out tight. Owner states Lexus corporate customer contact was dismissive of their complaints. Owner praises the strong performance.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner states the safety features give peace of mind on long trips. Owner finds the interior roomy, unlike the compact-feeling Cadillac CTS they compared it with. Owner praises the style. Owner states the price is comparable to other decent cars. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «not at all compact on interior»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a used ES 350 finds the infotainment complex, as if built for an engineer. Owner finds the front grille design unattractive. Owner praises the handling and responsiveness. Owner finds the fuel mileage good for a 300-plus-hp engine. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «built for an engineer»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Second-time ES 300h owner finds the electronics more complicated than in their 2013 model, though they are learning them. Owner praises the comfortable, great ride. Owner praises the luxurious interior. Owner praises the excellent gas mileage.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner finds many operations not intuitive and struggles to understand how features work. Owner praises the quietness. Owner praises the fuel economy.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner, who traded an RX 350 because of fuel costs, praises the 2021 ES 300h's mpg. Owner praises the power and handling in Sport mode. Owner values the reliability of the hybrid.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a new ES 300h praises the computer-assisted driving features. Owner likes the heated steering wheel. Owner likes the phone and app connectivity. Owner likes the styling of the car.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): New ES 300h owner praises the smooth ride. Owner praises the quiet ride.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): First-time hybrid owner states the ES 300h hybrid meets expectations and drives and rides well.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Third-time Lexus owner reports about 300 miles on roughly half a tank with the hybrid.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the fit and finish and interior, calling it nicer than a Mercedes and near Audi level, and says a Genesis G80 they tried felt like a cheap Hyundai. Owner finds the touchpad overly sensitive, though conventional controls exist for key functions. Owner states the hybrid drive is quiet but not suited to spirited driving. Owner praises the ride comfort. Owner praises the fuel mileage. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «overly sensitive»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner finds the hybrid quiet and responsive, running quietly up to about 45 mph. Owner praises the good mileage. Owner likes the phone, map and music connectivity. Owner likes the styling.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a used CT5 likes the exterior appearance. Owner likes the interior appearance. Owner praises the smooth, comfortable ride.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a new CT5 2.0T AWD reports plenty of acceleration. Owner praises the comfort. Owner likes the 'really nice options'. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «some really nice options»
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the styling. Owner likes the two-tone interior. Owner praises the value for money.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner finds the car roomy for a sports sedan. Owner finds the controls user-friendly and modern.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner likes the wireless phone charging pad. Owner calls the car's features user-friendly.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner finds the ride nice but not as nice as their previous Mercedes-Benz E300. Owner likes the many touch-pad features.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the ride. Owner praises the comfort. Owner likes the looks. Owner notes lots of bells and whistles and hopes to learn them all.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner states the wireless charger is hard to reach when a drink is in the cupholder. Owner states their knee hits the door handle while driving. Owner likes the rear backup camera screen. Owner likes the sporty, stylish looks.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the safety features. Owner calls it the most comfortable car they have had and likes the adjustable seat. Owner praises the roomy space.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner dislikes the black interior and the imitation-leather upholstery, which has a bad smell, and wants Cadillac to stop using that material. Owner likes the roominess. Owner states the car handles well and rides smoothly.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner describes a pleasant 750-mile drive completed in under 10 hours through a storm. Owner likes the looks of the car.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the handling and says the car is more fun to drive than the specs suggest. Owner praises the acceleration. Owner praises the body styling.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Former CT6 owner finds back-seat room limited, fine only for two people. Owner of their fifth Cadillac sedan states they like everything about the CT5.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner who wanted a sporty sedan likes the power of the turbo engine. Owner finds the car a little tight for larger passengers. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «a little tight»
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the smooth, comfortable ride. Owner likes the size and looks of the car. Owner likes the included upgrades.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Three-time Cadillac owner finds the new CUE infotainment system quicker and more responsive. Owner likes the ambient lighting. Owner states the materials and build quality are comparable to the German cars. Owner likes the auto-hold function. Owner likes the LED headlights. Owner likes the design. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «comparable to the German cars»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a new 2025 CT5 Sport finds it quick for a four-cylinder. Owner reports about 32 mpg on the highway. Owner likes the interior and its amenities. Owner states the CT5 is cheaper to maintain than European rivals (BMW not named). Owner finds the interior a little bit cramped.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Low-mileage owner of two 2025 CT5s finds the car too complicated, with many controls they do not understand. Owner complains the owner's manual runs over 450 pages and costs an extra $50. Owner reports no mechanical issues so far. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «the car is too hi-tech for me»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner states the acceleration is zippy. Owner praises the handling. Owner praises the self-driving features. Owner values the frequent software updates that improve the self-driving features. Owner states home charging is cheap; they keep the battery at 80%. Owner praises the audio system. Owner likes the ambient lighting. Owner likes the cooled (ventilated) seats.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (bought used, recommends the Long Range AWD) finds the car comfortable. Owner states the ride is quieter and more refined than the previous Model 3 and the car is fun to drive. Owner dislikes the lack of turn-signal stalks.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (former owner, bought used) calls it the best all-round car for its price point. Owner praises the savings on fuel costs. Owner praises the self-driving capability. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «All around best car for the price point.»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (Minnesota, bought new, does not recommend) finds the car uncomfortable. Owner states the car handles snow and rough roads poorly. Owner complains about the turning circle. Owner states the price is too high for the performance delivered. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «Uncomfortable and doesn't handle snow/bad road»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2024 Model 3 Performance states the car works well for family road trips. Owner praises the heated and ventilated front seats. Owner praises the rear-seat screen and controls for passengers. Owner likes the styling.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the suspension and calls the new Model 3 refined. Owner praises the sound system. Owner is happy with the range. Owner considers the pricing attractive. Owner likes the dual displays. Owner likes the exterior design. Owner states the stalkless controls are an easy adjustment.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner states the cabin is quieter. Owner praises the ventilated seats. Owner likes the solid feel of the doors. Owner likes the blind-spot indicators. Owner praises the acceleration. Owner likes one-pedal driving. Owner calls the removal of the turn-signal and drive-mode stalks the worst change in the refresh.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (does not recommend) reports poor comfort. Owner reports the car came with a locking problem. Owner states the car is not worth its price.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2025 Model 3 Performance (bought new, about 13k miles) praises the acceleration. Owner states the ride is quiet and smooth. Owner praises the sound system. Owner likes the smartphone app. Owner likes the camera system. Owner likes using self-driving in traffic. Owner reports a passenger door rattle that was fixed under warranty. Owner feels the paint is thin. Owner describes the minimalist interior as good quality overall.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2025 Model 3 Long Range (bought new, does not recommend) praises the acceleration. Owner values the Supercharger network. Owner likes the over-the-air updates. Owner likes controlling the car from the app. Owner states the interior feels cheap. Owner states the car feels rattly and loose on the road. Owner complains about poor cabin insulation. Owner complains about poor cabin air quality, citing odors. Owner dislikes the haptic buttons that replace the turn-signal stalks. Owner misses a head-up display. Owner reports significant phantom battery drain. Owner reports an incident while using Full Self-Driving. Owner objects to having to pay for upgrades that bring back removed features. Owner rates the car below their BMW i3 and plans to return it at lease end.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (bought new, about 2,000 miles) praises the smooth ride and how it absorbs bumps. Owner notes the improved interior materials. Owner says the infotainment is snappy. Owner finds the heated and ventilated seats comfortable. Owner reports no squeaks or rattles. Owner praises the storage space, including the front trunk. Owner states the missing turn-signal stalks are not a major issue. Owner praises the rear-seat screen.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a used 2022 Model S Plaid calls it the best car they have owned and praises its speed, comparing it with a Porsche 911 Cabriolet they previously owned. Owner praises the car's looks. Owner values that it seats five.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (second Tesla after a 2020 Model Y) reports no issues with the car. Owner complains that the car's resale value has fallen. Owner praises the latest version of Full Self-Driving. Owner says the yoke takes some getting used to because there is no turn-signal stalk.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (Toronto) praises the exterior design. Owner likes the lights. Owner praises the acceleration. Owner finds the interior too small for many people. Owner finds the price high. Owner considers reliability weak.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2022 Plaid bought new praises its performance and says it works as an everyday car and for road trips. Owner praises the build quality. Owner reports good experiences with the local Tesla service center. Owner considers it good value compared with gas-powered supercars. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «A SuperCar You Can Drive Everyday»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner says it took time to get used to the lack of buttons and the yoke. Owner likes the interior materials. Owner likes the exterior materials. Owner names quality control as the main complaint, citing a rear-seat rattle that Tesla fixed free of charge.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (bought new, does not recommend) praises the performance. Owner reports more than ten defects at delivery, including exposed wiring and peeling clearcoat. Owner finds the yoke poor for parking. Owner criticizes the lack of physical controls. Owner complains about slow service and no loaner cars. Owner reports phantom braking on Autopilot. Owner states the car is not worth its price. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «Exhilarating performance. Terrible build quality.»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the acceleration. Owner states the car is quiet. Owner praises the solid construction. Owner praises the range and the efficiency in winter. Owner notes the improved rear seating. Owner says total cost of ownership is lower than comparable gas cars despite the high upfront price. Owner says the yoke is growing on them for long drives but is frustrating when parking and in traffic circles because the turn signals are buttons rather than a stalk.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a used 2023 Model S (first Tesla) praises the performance. Owner praises the Full Self-Driving features while noting they are not perfect yet. Owner praises the large hatchback cargo area, comparing it with their Durango. Owner cites the value of buying a nearly two-year-old car rather than new.
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a 2023 Model S Plaid (Toronto) praises the acceleration, power, torque and top speed. Owner praises the interior space.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (bought new) praises the acceleration. Owner praises the quiet, composed cabin. Owner praises the air suspension. Owner likes driving mostly with one pedal. Owner likes the light steering. Owner likes the over-the-air software updates. Owner likes the built-in music-service integration (Apple Music, Spotify, Tidal). Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «Makes me grin with joy each time I start driving»
Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner praises the design. Owner praises the sound system.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner of a used 2021 Model S with the jet-style (yoke) wheel prefers its handling and driving feel to their Corvette. Owner praises the acceleration. Owner reports the battery was dead on delivery and the car had to be jump-started.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Owner (South Carolina, about 4 months, bought new) likes the driving feel and the choice of driver-preference settings. Owner likes that the navigation flags Supercharger locations along the route. Owner likes the elegant, hatchback-like design. Owner praises the ample storage space. Owner finds the seats fine for everyday driving but less comfortable on long trips, and uses a seat cushion. Owner states the range (377 miles on the window sticker) drops in cold weather and improves with efficient driving and warmer weather.
